note: v1 98.65 (seeds 0/11 98.65/98.64), first draft of MODERN MINIMAL, 'Both Ways', for The Endless Stair - featured illusion THE TRITONE PARADOX (Diana Deutsch). Two Shepard tones a tritone apart have no true direction: the second is exactly as far above the first as below it, so some listeners hear the pair rise and others fall, depending on where the tones' spectral envelope sits. Each bar plays a step of THE STAIR (Eb F Gb Bb) answered by its tritone (A B C E); through the track two copies of the pairs cross-fade from a low-centred envelope (250 Hz) to a high-centred one (1 kHz), so for many ears the stair turns round; in the break the Shepard position glides up an octave under them, and in the last groove both envelopes play at once - it goes both ways. Under it: a rolling sixteenth bass through a ladder breathing on 5- and 7-bar LFOs, crisp machine drums, dub stabs on Ebm9 - Cbmaj7 - Abm9 - Bbm7. 122.5 -> 123 ramped, -11.0 LUFS, true peak -1.3. Seams drafted with t10 and t12.
rebaselined on compscore 898ec630: v1 (the song file) scores 95.587/95.572 on seeds 0/11; best was 98.65 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v2 95.22 (seeds 0/11 95.22/95.27, level with v1 re-scored 95.25/95.23): the same seam fix as The Ghost Note. The render added 1.3 s of release tail after the last bar, so the three seconds a DJ mixes out of into t12 were half silence; the song now ends on its last bar (tail 0.1 s). The join to The Ghost Note drops 7.2 -> 5.3 dB; the tritone pair's last notes still ring into t12's intro. Kept on judgment (the totals are level): a continuous tape needs every track to end where its music ends.

v3 95.23 (seed 0, level with the current version re-scored at 95.15): the seam-tempo fix (chirper-zero's finding, now that the groove overlaps neighbours for 16 bars). The tempo ramp used to run from the first beat to the last, so each 16-bar overlap was still drifting under the neighbour's fixed tempo; now the intro holds the incoming seam tempo and the ramp finishes as the outro starts, so both overlaps sit at one tempo and the kicks never flam. No change to the music; compscore can't hear it, the live mix can.

v4 95.78 (seeds 0/11 95.78/95.76 vs v3 re-scored 94.83/94.82): room for the paradox. Both Ways sat 8 dB heavy at 340-470 Hz - the low-centred Shepard pairs and the dub stabs on top of each other - and 8-11 dB short at 2-3.6 kHz. The stabs are now high-passed at 220 Hz and open from 2.8 to 4.2 kHz, the master's low-mid dip deepens from -2 to -4 dB at 380 Hz, and the presence lift goes from +5 to +7 dB at 3.2 kHz, so the low-centred pairs (the illusion's first answer) have the low-mids to themselves and the minimal top end is crisp. Spectrum 88 -> 95; flow from t10 improves too (spectral 7.9 -> 6.7). Tried and not kept: a deeper break (-7 dB) - level with v3.

v5 95.81 (seeds 0/11 95.81/95.79 vs v4 re-scored 95.78/95.76): THE KEY GOES BOTH WAYS - playing with key around the illusion. Both Ways' hook is the tritone paradox, a pair with no up or down; now, for eight bars in the middle of the last groove, the whole harmony moves a tritone - E-flat minor to A minor, as far from home as a key can go and just as far up as down. The sub, the rolling bass and the stabs all move; the Shepard pairs move with them, and a tritone pair moved a tritone is the same two notes the other way round (Eb/A becomes A/Eb), so the question stays exactly where it was while the ground under it turns. Home for the last eight bars and the outro, so the seam into The Ghost Note is untouched. Measured, not heard: the form still reads 14-15 sections, spectrum and every other term level or up.
